goal: DEPTH: sub-sections / config sections in real integration with the backend — raise real coverage and capability levels
must_build: Every page in ui-spec/azure/aks.json (37 pages; nav: Overview, Activity log, Access control (IAM), Tags, Diagnose and solve problems, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Kubernetes resources, Settings, Monitoring, Automation, Help)
Backend: ARM Microsoft.ContainerService managedClusters + node pools
List / create / detail / edit / delete round-trips through the native API the SDK and CLI use
always: Every page wired to the native API on /_wire (no static data); liveness fixtures for every list/detail page
core/capabilities/azure/aks.json: one entry per console section with an honest level + tests; tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py must pass
Capability feature ids MUST start with 'azure.' (e.g. 'azure.aks.<section>') — ids share one namespace with the AWS registry
Read the 'Cloud lenses' section of consoles/AGENT-UI.md first — use this cloud's kit, not Cloudscape

depth_targets.title: Start / Stop cluster
limitations: Start/Stop update the cluster's logical powerState only — there are no real node VMs in-browser to deallocate or boot, so no compute cost changes and no API server downtime are actually simulated.

depth_targets.title: Run command (az aks command invoke)
limitations: Vyomi does not run a real kubelet or API server, so runCommand accepts and echoes the submitted command in its response but never actually executes it against a live cluster.

depth_targets.title: listClusterUserCredential / listClusterAdminCredential (kubeconfig)
limitations: The returned kubeconfig is shaped like the real response (cluster/user/context pointing at the cluster's fqdn) but its certificate and token material is a fixed placeholder, and the server address accepts no real kubectl connections.

depth_targets.title: Kubernetes namespaces (create, list, delete)
limitations: Namespaces are modelled as a stateful list on the cluster resource (seeded with the real default/kube-system/kube-public/kube-node-lease set a fresh cluster ships with) — Vyomi stores and returns them exactly as written, but nothing is scheduled into a namespace because there is no live Kubernetes API server behind it.

depth_targets.title: Live Kubernetes objects (Workloads, Services and ingresses, Storage, Configuration, Custom resources, Events)
limitations: These panels proxy kubectl/the Kubernetes API server of the cluster itself (not ARM) — Vyomi does not run a kubelet or API server in-browser, so pods, deployments, services and other live cluster objects are not simulated.

depth_targets.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.
